workload: One listening-post waterfall frame of HackRF CU8 at 20 Msps and 25 fps (800000 I/Q pairs), the buffer fft_reader passes to cu8_to_complex.
notes: The conversion astype's the whole byte buffer to float32, subtracts and divides into further full-size arrays, then copies both strided I and Q slices before building complex64. Scaling blocks straight into the result's float view keeps the traced peak at the 6.4MB output instead of 19.2MB, and the samples stay identical.

workload: Amplitude columns for a 2 second Sub-GHz inspect window after decimation to 1 MS/s (2000000 complex64 samples), the maximum window inspect_window will plot.
notes: np.abs allocates a full float amplitude array before the column max. Taking the max in blocks produces the same 40000-column list and drops the traced peak from about 9.5MB to about 1.6MB.

workload: 800 updates of one device holding the steady-state 300-sample RSSI buffer (MAX_RSSI_SAMPLES), which is one second of advertisements from about 80 nearby devices.
notes: Every advertisement recomputes statistics.median and statistics.variance over all 300 integer samples, and _calculate_confidence computes the variance again with exact Fraction arithmetic. A single sum-of-squares pass matches that variance exactly on integer RSSI and is about 3.5x faster on this buffer.

workload: One correlation pass over 200 Wi-Fi and 200 Bluetooth devices with ISO timestamps, as in a busy-office TSCM refresh where the two populations do not overlap in time.
notes: _to_observation parses each Bluetooth device's timestamps inside the Wi-Fi loop, so every device is parsed once per pair. Parsing both sides once is local to correlate and about halves this 200x200 pass; caching the lowercased manufacturer and OUI in that same function removes the remaining per-pair string work.
